purpose: WH-054 packet 1a classification of every column that references users(id). Proposed engineering classification; nothing is accepted. Two owner answers recorded in the contract on October 8, 2026 (member-only accounts, the five-active-member limit) are copied onto their questions; they change no entry's class or status, and the four remaining product questions are open. The schema freeze (packet 1b) is refused while any entry is not accepted or any question is open.

classes.account: Keeps REFERENCES users; deleted with the person.
classes.workspace: Tenant data; becomes workspace_id REFERENCES workspaces.
classes.workspace+actor: Tenant data plus a pseudonymous actor_ref that survives person deletion.
classes.workspace+custody: Tenant-usable provider credential or consent; the authorizing actor is recorded separately from the tenant.
classes.workspace+payer: Billing record attached to the workspace with payer-of-record provenance kept separate from the actor.
classes.typed-subject: One current column becomes two typed columns (account_id / workspace_id) with an exclusive-or check.
classes.split: One current column and table become two tables, one per subject type.

statuses.proposed: Engineering classification awaiting the child-1 schema review. Not frozen, not approved.
statuses.undecided: The class or key cannot be accepted until the named owner question is answered. The class shown is the working proposal.
statuses.accepted: Reserved for the child-1 schema review. No entry is accepted at this baseline.

evidenceLevels.review-spike: Classified by the October 8 feasibility review. The in-memory spike was one mechanical key rename with 22 schema-wide assertions (19 passed); it did not exercise this entry's disposition, so the entry is not fixture-proven.
evidenceLevels.source-reading: Proposed from repository source reading only; no fixture or test has exercised the disposition.

vocabulary.roles: tenant, account, actor, custody, payer and epoch are separate roles on separate intended columns; none stands in for another. account keeps REFERENCES users; the others never reference users.

retargets.hand-written: The tenant column is re-keyed in hand-written canonical inputs. A mechanical RENAME COLUMN is not valid (three renames failed in the spike and at least 22 bodies stayed silently wrong).
retargets.typed-subject: Two new typed columns; not a uniform retarget.
retargets.split: Two new tables; not a uniform retarget.

questions.summary: Who is the payer of record after a transfer, and what the recipient must do before completion.

ownerAnswer.answer: A person with a completed account may join and use an invited workspace without first creating their own workspace or project; member-only accounts are allowed.

questions.summary: Whether a person holding only memberships may enter without creating a workspace.
Retention of suspended rows, workspace audit, actor rows, invitations and the provider login in terminal revocation receipts (GitHub login included); closure cancellation window.

ownerAnswer.answer: The first release permits five active members per workspace, including owners. It is an initial capacity limit, not a pricing commitment.

questions.summary: Whether the engineering default of 5 active members counts owners, and whether pricing copy may mention a limit.
How late a renewal may be recorded and still keep members without an owner resume (settlement window).
Bound on platform-funded budgets and project quota across the workspaces one account may own or fund (not the first workspace of a member-only account, which follows ordinary creation rules).
